The 14:10–14:15 segment is in any event justified under RD-4: the optimal route on Orchard Road was at speed band 1 (0–9 km/h) during 14:00–14:10 (F15) and an LTA-reported accident with two lanes closed lay 0 m from that route, reported 13:52, before the segment and during the trip window (F18); no incident is recorded anywhere near the far-flung segment F5, which is why the driver only claims the exemption for F4.

The rider did agree to a stop, but only generically — 'Can you stop at a 7-Eleven on the way?' (F11) named no location — and the only stop of the trip, 4 min 10 s at 14:20–14:24 (F2), sits 2995 m from pickup and 2098 m from drop-off on the far segment F5, so the stop is not evidence that the F5 detour itself was authorised.

Because the driver accepts that segment F5 (14:17–14:29, +2.87 km, up to 1553 m off the optimal route) was not covered by any rider message before it began, the only fair result for the excess-distance component is the RD-2 metered measure of that segment: 2.87 km × $1.41/km = $4.05, i.e. a partial refund capped at about $4.05, which is less than the $7.99 of billed excess distance (F6) the rider's complaint targets.

The remaining billed items are regular metered RydeTAXI components: $1.08 of waiting time for the 4.2-minute stop (F7), which RD-3(c) leaves payable on a metered taxi, and total charges of $25.81 with no surge (F8) — nothing here is an unpublished add-on of the kind FARE-1 removes.

The driver's 90-day record (1 upheld dispute, no-show only) does not meet the RD-6 trigger, because the only upheld matter is not a route matter and this case is the driver's first upheld route dispute.
No message in the record is threatening, intimidating or harassing, and no dangerous-driving or injury allegation appears anywhere in the record, so SAFE-1/SAFE-2 escalation is not engaged.

weaknesses: The driver's own written statement that he 'stopped at the 7-Eleven I know on Beach Road' (F14) is a driver-side claim: the chat (F10–F13) never names Beach Road or any 7-Eleven location, and the rider's message (F11) named no place, so the other side will argue the whole Beach Road leg was the driver's own errand and is written off as RD-1 unexcused distance — 144% over the optimal distance (F1) and 18.8 minutes late (F3).

The stay-put point for F5 is bad for the driver: 4 min 10 s stationary 2995 m from pickup and 2098 m from drop-off (F2), which is exactly what the rider will use to prove the 14:17–14:29 loop (F5, +2.87 km) reached nowhere the rider asked for, rather than a mere 'on the way' 7-Eleven stop.

The named-road chain for F4 is inferential: F18 only places the accident on Orchard Road 'after Cavenagh Road' and no fact places the car on Cavenagh Road or names a road inside segment F4, so the judge may find the F4 consent untied (G13 / RD-5) and refund the full 4.72 km, about $6.66 rather than $4.05.

events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $5.05 (model confidence 0.72)
events.body:
CASE C-0001: metered RydeTAXI, Orchard Road → Marina Bay Sands, billed $25.81 [F9]. Two off-route segments exist [F4][F5], so RD-1 applies and each is screened separately [RD-1]. F4 (14:10–14:15, +1.85 km) is exempt: the trace settles RD-4(a) with an LTA-recorded accident on Orchard Road at 13:52, 0 m from the replaced stretch of the optimal route, reported before the segment and inside the trip window [F18][F15][RD-4]. RD-4 is a sufficient ground, so I need not reach the contested RD-5 reading of the same exchange; the rider's "Sure." [F11] answers the driver's 14:01 ask [F10], but F4 stands exempt on the incident ground alone, and any residual question about Cavenagh's tie is immaterial.

F5 (14:17–14:29, +2.87 km, up to 1553 m off route) receives no RD-4 excuse: the trace marks ✗ for it, and the alternate corridor was free-flowing (Bras Basah band 4 [F16], Bayfront band 3 [F17]), so congestion does not cover it [RD-4(c)]. On the argued grounds, I read the rider's words [F11][F10] as a general route choice plus a stop request; on either reading — rider-named stop under RD-3 or named-road consent under RD-5 — the segment counts. The stop the car actually made is 4 min 10 s stationary at a point 2995 m from pickup and 2098 m from drop-off [F2], and the only record placing that stop anywhere is the driver's own post-trip statement naming his 7-Eleven "on Beach Road" [F14]. A driver statement naming another place is not consent (G11) and places the segment away from the agreed path: agreeing to "go round by Cavenagh" never covers a trip to a far shop [RD-5]. The rider's message named no place ("a 7-Eleven on the way" [F11]), so RD-3(a) does not exempt the driver's choice of a distant one — it counts. F5 is unexempted [RD-1].

Refund is the metered measure on the Rubicon of the trip's own rate: $13.55 ÷ 9.61 km = $1.4100/km [F9][F6]; 2.87 km × $1.4100/km = $4.047 ≈ $4.05 [F5][F6][RD-2]. F4's 1.85 km is exempt, so it is excluded despite being over-billed (the total billed excess of 5.67 km / $7.99 [F6] is not the refund base). The stop's metered waiting charge $1.08 (4.2 min × $0.26/min) [F7][F9] stays payable on a metered taxi [RD-3(c)], and I find no unpublished add-on to remove under FARE-1 [F9]. The billed excess outside F4/F5 (0.95 km) is not attributable to any segment and is not refunded [RD-2].

RD-6 is not triggered: route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 [F21], the one upheld 90-day matter being a no-show; the trace marks ✗, so no flag_account [RD-6]. Safety screen: I read every chat message [F10][F11][F12], the driver statement [F14] and the complaint; nothing threatening, intimidating, harassing, sexual or dangerous-driving related — this is a fare/route dispute [SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. The chat record is complete and fully timestamped [F13], GPS covers both segments and the stop [F2][F4][F5], and the fare record gives the rate [F6][F9], so the record settles every element the ruling needs.

events.title: Ruling verification against the policy certificate
events.body: ✗ amount 5.05 ≠ formula 4.05
certificate: ✓ RD-1 off-route segment(s) exist [case] 2 segment(s) (F4, F5)
✓ RD-4 (a) incident on the replaced stretch, reported before the detour [F4] incident within 300 m of optimal km 0.8–1.6 (F18)
– RD-5 consent scope [F4] not needed: RD-4 already exempts this segment (no evidence)
– RD-3 rider-requested stop [F4] not needed: RD-4 already exempts this segment (no evidence)
✗ RD-4 (a) incident on the replaced stretch, reported before the detour [F5] no qualifying incident (speed band alone does not exempt) (F18)

? RD-5 rider agreed to this route before the detour; scope of that agreement [F5] RULE: exempt only if a RIDER message sent before 14:17:45 agrees AND the agreement covers this segment. Three kinds of agreement: (1) GENERAL route choice ('take whichever way is faster') covers a route chosen to get there, not an errand of the driver's own (a stop away from the route, a loop that reaches nothing: counts). (2) A SPECIFIC named road or area ('go round via X') covers driving on X only: the record must tie this segment to X (a stop on X, a message placing the car on X, a road name in a fact); timing alone does not, and the fact table carries no road names for the driven path — if nothing ties them, the finding is undetermined (G13); if the record places this segment somewhere else (a stop away from X, the driver's own statement naming another road or place, a stop the driver chose the location of), the agreement to X does not cover it: counts. (3) Scope unclear: undetermined. A driver's claim of agreement that appears only in his statement is not consent (G11); a complete chat record with no rider agreement before the segment: counts. This finding changes the amount. Evidence — F10: Chat #1 14:01 driver: “Hi, traffic on Orchard is bad, ok if I go round by Cavenagh?”; F11: Chat #2 14:02 rider: “Sure. Can you stop at a 7-Eleven on the way?”; F12: Chat #3 14:03 driver: “Ok”; F14: Driver statement (written after the trip, not part of the chat): “Orchard was jammed after an accident, rider agreed to go round by Cavenagh and asked for a stop. I stopped at the 7-Eleven I know on Beach Road.” (F10, F11, F12, F14)

? A stop the rider asked for without naming a place ('a 7-Eleven on the way') does not excuse the driver's choice of a far one → counts. Stops in this segment: F2. (F10, F11, F12, F2)

ruling.reasoning:
CASE C-0001: metered RydeTAXI, Orchard Road → Marina Bay Sands, billed $25.81 [F9]. Two off-route segments exist [F4][F5], so RD-1 applies and each is screened separately [RD-1]. F4 (14:10–14:15, +1.85 km) is exempt: the trace settles RD-4(a) with an LTA-recorded accident on Orchard Road at 13:52, 0 m from the replaced stretch of the optimal route, reported before the segment and inside the trip window [F18][F15][RD-4]. RD-4 is a sufficient ground, so I need not reach the contested RD-5 reading of the same exchange; the rider's "Sure." [F11] answers the driver's 14:01 ask [F10], but F4 stands exempt on the incident ground alone, and any residual question about Cavenagh's tie is immaterial.

F5 (14:17–14:29, +2.87 km, up to 1553 m off route) receives no RD-4 excuse: the trace marks ✗ for it, and the alternate corridor was free-flowing (Bras Basah band 4 [F16], Bayfront band 3 [F17]), so congestion does not cover it [RD-4(c)]. On the argued grounds, I read the rider's words [F11][F10] as a general route choice plus a stop request; on either reading — rider-named stop under RD-3 or named-road consent under RD-5 — the segment counts. The stop the car actually made is 4 min 10 s stationary at a point 2995 m from pickup and 2098 m from drop-off [F2], and the only record placing that stop anywhere is the driver's own post-trip statement naming his 7-Eleven "on Beach Road" [F14]. A driver statement naming another place is not consent (G11) and places the segment away from the agreed path: agreeing to "go round by Cavenagh" never covers a trip to a far shop [RD-5]. The rider's message named no place ("a 7-Eleven on the way" [F11]), so RD-3(a) does not exempt the driver's choice of a distant one — it counts. F5 is unexempted [RD-1].

Refund is the metered measure on the Rubicon of the trip's own rate: $13.55 ÷ 9.61 km = $1.4100/km [F9][F6]; 2.87 km × $1.4100/km = $4.047 ≈ $4.05 [F5][F6][RD-2]. F4's 1.85 km is exempt, so it is excluded despite being over-billed (the total billed excess of 5.67 km / $7.99 [F6] is not the refund base). The stop's metered waiting charge $1.08 (4.2 min × $0.26/min) [F7][F9] stays payable on a metered taxi [RD-3(c)], and I find no unpublished add-on to remove under FARE-1 [F9]. The billed excess outside F4/F5 (0.95 km) is not attributable to any segment and is not refunded [RD-2].

RD-6 is not triggered: route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 [F21], the one upheld 90-day matter being a no-show; the trace marks ✗, so no flag_account [RD-6]. Safety screen: I read every chat message [F10][F11][F12], the driver statement [F14] and the complaint; nothing threatening, intimidating, harassing, sexual or dangerous-driving related — this is a fare/route dispute [SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. The chat record is complete and fully timestamped [F13], GPS covers both segments and the stop [F2][F4][F5], and the fare record gives the rate [F6][F9], so the record settles every element the ruling needs.

claims.assertion: The trip ran 9.6 km against a 3.9 km optimal route (+5.7 km, +144%) in 26.5 min against a 7.7 min estimate, and the record contains two off-route segments with 1.85 km and 2.87 km of extra distance; under RD-1 each segment is assessed separately and any segment not exempted is an unexempted deviation.

The rider's only route-related message expresses a general route choice: at 14:01 the driver asked 'Hi, traffic on Orchard is bad, ok if I go round by Cavenagh?' and the rider answered at 14:02 'Sure. Can you stop at a 7-Eleven on the way?' — a general assent plus a stop request, not a selection of a named road, and 'Cavenagh' appears only in the driver's own ask, with no record tying either driven segment to Cavenagh Road.

The first off-route segment (14:10–14:15, +1.85 km) began after the rider's 14:02 message but the record never places the car on a named road; if the judge reads the short 'Sure' as assent to Cavenagh Road it is still untied, because no stop, positioning message or road-name fact ties this segment to Cavenagh Road (G13), and no rider message names any other route for this segment.

The second off-route segment (14:17–14:29, +2.87 km, up to 1553 m off the optimal route) contains a 4 min 10 s stationary period at 14:20–14:24 at coordinates 2995 m from the pickup and 2098 m from the drop-off, i.e. not a pickup or drop-off point; this stop was the driver's own errand at the '7-Eleven I know on Beach Road' — a place the rider never named — so it is outside any consent and generates the segment's extra km.

The driver's post-trip statement claims 'Orchard was jammed after an accident, rider agreed to go round by Cavenagh and asked for a stop. I stopped at the 7-Eleven I know on Beach Road'; the only accident record is a single incident at one point on Orchard Road, which cannot justify a 5.7 km detour, and the rider's spoken agreement cannot supply consent that the chat does not show (G11).

Traffic on the optimal corridor does not justify the deviation as a whole: Orchard Road was band 1 (0–9 km/h) only for 14:00–14:10, while Bras Basah Road was band 4 (30–39 km/h) for 14:00–14:35 and Bayfront Avenue band 3 (20–29 km/h) from 14:20 — so the alternate corridor was largely free-flowing and the second off-route segment cannot be excused by congestion.
This is a metered RydeTAXI trip, so the 5.67 km of excess distance was billed at the trip's per-km rate: excess distance billed $7.99 (5.67 km × $1.41/km).

The unexempted segments' extra km are 1.85 km (F4) and 2.87 km (F5), totalling 4.72 km, which at the trip's per-km rate of $1.41/km (F6) gives 4.72 × $1.41 = $6.6552, i.e. $6.66 refundable under RD-2; the remaining 0.95 km of the billed excess (5.67 − 4.72) is not attributable to any segment and is not claimed.

The in-trip stop also produced a $1.08 metered waiting charge (4.2 min × $0.26/min); that waiting time is recorded on the meter and RD-3(c) leaves RydeTAXI waiting time on the meter, so this $1.08 is not claimed as a refund.

The driver already has 1 upheld no-show dispute in the last 90 days and 3 disputes in total; if the judge finds RD-2 refund > 0 here, RD-6 makes this case a repeated violation and warrants a flag_account referral for Ryde account review.

weaknesses: The rider's 14:02 message 'Sure.' does follow the driver's 14:01 ask that names Cavenagh Road; the driver will argue that under RD-5 this is a specific named-road consent (named_road_tied/untied), which would exempt at least the first off-route segment (F4) and cut the claim to about the second segment's 2.87 km ≈ $4.05.

There is a genuine traffic record: an accident on Orchard Road at 13:52 with two lanes closed, 0 m from the optimal route (F18), plus Orchard Road band 1 congestion 14:00–14:10 (F15); the driver will argue RD-4(a) excuse, though it is a single point on the optimal route and the alternate corridor was fast (F16, F17).

The 4 min 10 s stop (F2) shows the car stopped somewhere away from the corridor, but no fact names the road at that location; my claim that it is Beach Road rests on the driver's own statement (F14), so the judge may find the segment-road link undetermined (G13).

The refund is capped by the metered-distance method: 0.95 km of billed excess (5.67 − 4.72) and the $1.08 waiting fee (F7) are not recoverable under RD-2/RD-3(c), so the maximum realistic recovery is $6.66 of the $25.81 charged.

claims.assertion: The segment 14:10–14:15 (F4) was covered by a named-road consent: at 14:01 the driver asked 'ok if I go round by Cavenagh?' (F10) and the rider answered 'Sure.' at 14:02 (F11), i.e. before the segment began, and the record ties that name to the ride because the accident closing two lanes sat 0 m from the optimal route on Orchard Road 'after Cavenagh Road' (F18), so Cavenagh Road is the junction from which the detour round the closure begins.

The 14:10–14:15 segment is in any event justified under RD-4: the optimal route on Orchard Road was at speed band 1 (0–9 km/h) during 14:00–14:10 (F15) and an LTA-reported accident with two lanes closed lay 0 m from that route, reported 13:52, before the segment and during the trip window (F18); no incident is recorded anywhere near the far-flung segment F5, which is why the driver only claims the exemption for F4.

The rider did agree to a stop, but only generically — 'Can you stop at a 7-Eleven on the way?' (F11) named no location — and the only stop of the trip, 4 min 10 s at 14:20–14:24 (F2), sits 2995 m from pickup and 2098 m from drop-off on the far segment F5, so the stop is not evidence that the F5 detour itself was authorised.

Because the driver accepts that segment F5 (14:17–14:29, +2.87 km, up to 1553 m off the optimal route) was not covered by any rider message before it began, the only fair result for the excess-distance component is the RD-2 metered measure of that segment: 2.87 km × $1.41/km = $4.05, i.e. a partial refund capped at about $4.05, which is less than the $7.99 of billed excess distance (F6) the rider's complaint targets.

The remaining billed items are regular metered RydeTAXI components: $1.08 of waiting time for the 4.2-minute stop (F7), which RD-3(c) leaves payable on a metered taxi, and total charges of $25.81 with no surge (F8) — nothing here is an unpublished add-on of the kind FARE-1 removes.

The driver's 90-day record (1 upheld dispute, no-show only) does not meet the RD-6 trigger, because the only upheld matter is not a route matter and this case is the driver's first upheld route dispute.
No message in the record is threatening, intimidating or harassing, and no dangerous-driving or injury allegation appears anywhere in the record, so SAFE-1/SAFE-2 escalation is not engaged.

weaknesses: The driver's own written statement that he 'stopped at the 7-Eleven I know on Beach Road' (F14) is a driver-side claim: the chat (F10–F13) never names Beach Road or any 7-Eleven location, and the rider's message (F11) named no place, so the other side will argue the whole Beach Road leg was the driver's own errand and is written off as RD-1 unexcused distance — 144% over the optimal distance (F1) and 18.8 minutes late (F3).

The stay-put point for F5 is bad for the driver: 4 min 10 s stationary 2995 m from pickup and 2098 m from drop-off (F2), which is exactly what the rider will use to prove the 14:17–14:29 loop (F5, +2.87 km) reached nowhere the rider asked for, rather than a mere 'on the way' 7-Eleven stop.

The named-road chain for F4 is inferential: F18 only places the accident on Orchard Road 'after Cavenagh Road' and no fact places the car on Cavenagh Road or names a road inside segment F4, so the judge may find the F4 consent untied (G13 / RD-5) and refund the full 4.72 km, about $6.66 rather than $4.05.

The traffic excuse only covers the Orchard Road stretch (F15 band 1, F16 Bras Basah band 4, F18 accident at 0 m), and the judge may read the 26.5-minute, 9.6 km ride as a single course of conduct rather than two severable segments, which would inflate the driver's exposure.

points.response: The exchange is an offer plus a short assent, not a rider's choice of a road: the rider's own words add an unrelated stop request ('Can you stop at a 7-Eleven on the way?', F11) and no record places the car on Cavenagh Road, so at best the F4 consent is untied (G13, RD-5); F18 carries the name only inside the incident description ('accident on Orchard Road after Cavenagh Road'), which is not a fact tying the F4 segment to Cavenagh Road.

F18 is one accident point on the optimal route reported 13:52, and F15's band 1 (0–9 km/h) on Orchard Road covers only 14:00–14:10 while the alternate corridor was free-flowing (Bras Basah band 4, 30–39 km/h, F16), so the record does not show the replaced stretch of optimal route was blocked; at most RD-4 excuses that stretch, and the F4 segment still added 1.85 km reaching up to 803 m off the optimal route (F4).

Conceded on this narrow point: the rider's message named no place (F11), so the stop request itself does not authorise the F5 loop, and we do not rely on it as consent — we rely on the opposite, that the 4 min 10 s stationary period (F2) shows an errand the rider never asked for, which is why the segment's extra km stays billable under RD-5.

The driver's concession covers only F5; F4's 1.85 km (F4) is likewise unexempted because the consent is untied (G13) and the traffic excuse reaches only the replaced stretch, so the metered measure is the full 4.72 km × $1.41/km = $6.66 (F4, F5, F6), not $4.05.

Not disputed as to the $1.08 metered waiting (F7) and the absence of surge (F8); we claim no unpublished add-on under FARE-1, only the metered excess distance for the unexempted segments, so the driver's own concession of $4.05 is the floor and $6.66 the correct figure.

RD-6's trigger is a 90-day history of an upheld dispute plus a case found against the driver, and F21 shows 1 upheld dispute in 90 d and 3 disputes in total; if the judge finds any unexempted distance here, the wording 'repeated' permits the flag_account referral even though the prior upheld matter was a no-show.

No safety escalation is sought; we note only that the 7.7-minute estimated trip took 26.5 minutes and the recorded loop reached 1553 m from the optimal route (F3, F5), which is why the distance, not any safety clause, decides this case.

Not contested: the two off-route segments F4 (14:10–14:15, +1.85 km) and F5 (14:17–14:29, +2.87 km) are each reviewed separately under RD-1 and the driver contests only the ground of F4, not the existence of the excess distance.

The exchange is a driver ask naming a road ('ok if I go round by Cavenagh?', F10) answered by the rider 'Sure.' at 14:02, before the F4 segment began at 14:10, which under RD-5 is an answer to the named road, not a general 'whichever way is faster' delegation; and the record ties Cavenagh Road to the ride because the 13:52 incident with two lanes closed sits after Cavenagh Road on the optimal Orchard Road route, 0 m off it (F18).

The tie the opponent says is missing is F18 itself: the road the rider agreed to, Cavenagh Road, is the point at which the closed two-lane stretch on the optimal Orchard Road route begins, so the only way round the Orchard Road closure that existed (F15, F18) is the Cavenagh turning the rider accepted; if the judge still finds the F4 link to that road insufficient, the honest result is named_road_untied, not a violation any wider than that segment.

The driver does not resist this segment: the 4 min 10 s stop at 14:20–14:24 (F2) sits inside the F5 loop 2995 m from pickup, and the rider's only stop request named no place (F11), so the driver's own statement that he chose the '7-Eleven I know on Beach Road' (F14) makes F5, not F4, the unexempted deviation and limits the refund accordingly.

No consent is claimed from the driver's after-trip statement; F4 rests on the rider's own 14:02 message, and the accident record F18 is the RD-4 evidence — reported 13:52, 0 m from the optimal route and within the trip window — which excuses only the segment around the closure (F4), not the whole 5.7 km the opponent attributes to it.

The driver claims congestion only for F4, where Orchard Road on the optimal route was band 1 (0–9 km/h) in 14:00–14:10 (F15) with the F18 accident closing two of its lanes, and expressly concedes that free-flowing Bras Basah (F16, band 4) and Bayfront (F17, band 3) give no excuse for F5.

The $6.66 figure double-counts the segment the rider accepted: on the driver's reading F4 is exempt under RD-5/RD-4, so only F5's 2.87 km is refundable at the trip rate of $1.41/km read off F6, giving 2.87 × $1.41 = $4.05.

RD-6 does not reach this driver: the single upheld matter in F21 is a no-show, not a route dispute, and F21 records zero upheld route cases, so this trip cannot be made 'repeated' by an unrelated matter.
